newsitem.title: GERMANY: France wants stability pact - Germany's Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: France wants stability pact - Germany's Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday France would keep to the stability pact, adhere to the strict criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) and join the planned launch of Europe's single currency on time.

In the text of a government statement to the German lower house of parliament, Kinkel said Germany was prepared to agree to a jobs chapter at a European Union summit in Amsterdam next week as long as this did not incur extra EU spending.

"It (France) will adhere to the stability pact and -- just like the German government -- it will launch the euro on time according to stability criteria," Kinkel said. the speech was due to be followed by a parliamentary debate about next week's European Union summit in Amsterdam.
Kinkel said Bonn would agree to a jobs chapter to be added to the Maastricht treaty, signalling a policy change. But he added this would only be on condition this did not involve additional spending.

"We do not want any unaccountable, unfinanceable or expensive spending programmes. An improved coordination of national measures on European level can take us further. Under this sign, the German government will agree to a jobs chapter.

Germany had opposed the idea of a jobs chapter for years, fearing it could lead to economic growth-led policies that in turn would counteract the monetary discipline a future independent European central bank would seek to impose.
Kinkel warned all those who express doubts that Europe's planned single currency, the euro, would not come into being.

"Those who support a delay (in EMU) must realise they will bring about an end of this ambitious project and those (who support delay) must also realise they are doing enormous damage to our country," Kinkel said.
